boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: Ten named SDSU study settings, each selected for a documented workspace feature or access detail.

cards.title: Avera Health and Science Center
cards.subtitle: First- and third-floor study spots near College Green
cards.notes: Choose the first floor for varied table sizes and nearby vending, or head to the third floor for natural light and large collaborative tables.
cards.short_summary: A two-floor option that separates table variety from bright, collaborative work.
cards.evidence_claim: SDSU identifies study spots on the first and third floors; the third floor has natural lighting, low volume and large collaborative tables.
cards.source_title: Campus Study Rooms and Spaces | South Dakota State University
cards.access_notes: SDSU lists these as campus study spots; no reservation information is stated.

cards.entity_name: Chicoine Architecture, Mathematics and Engineering Hall
cards.title: Chicoine Architecture, Mathematics and Engineering Hall
cards.subtitle: Second- and third-floor study areas on south campus
cards.notes: Use the second-floor nooks for whiteboard tables and outlets, or move upstairs for a lower-volume setting with natural light and whiteboard tables.
cards.short_summary: Whiteboard-table study nooks with outlet access on two floors.
cards.evidence_claim: SDSU lists second- and third-floor study spaces with whiteboard tables and outlets; the third floor also has natural lighting and low traffic.
cards.source_title: Campus Study Rooms and Spaces | South Dakota State University
cards.access_notes: SDSU lists the Math Help Center and study nooks on the second floor; no reservation requirement is stated.

cards.entity_name: The Fish-Bowl at Crothers Engineering Hall
cards.title: The Fish-Bowl at Crothers Engineering Hall
cards.subtitle: First floor, east side of Crothers Engineering Hall
cards.notes: Set up near the first-floor east side when you want daylight, furniture outlets and computer-lab access in the same named open study area.
cards.short_summary: An open, daylight-oriented study area with power and nearby lab access.
cards.evidence_claim: SDSU states that the Fish-Bowl is open to all students and provides natural lighting, furniture outlets, vending and computer-lab access.
cards.source_title: Campus Study Rooms and Spaces | South Dakota State University
cards.access_notes: Open to all students; located on the first floor's east side.

cards.title: Harding Hall
cards.subtitle: Study areas across all three floors
cards.notes: Pick the entryway for mixed seating and a casting-capable monitor, or use upper-floor collaborative rooms for whiteboards, outlets and casting TVs.
cards.short_summary: A building-wide study choice with both quick-stop seating and small collaborative rooms.
cards.evidence_claim: SDSU lists low-volume study spaces on all three floors, including whiteboards, natural lighting, outlets and casting-capable screens.
cards.source_title: Campus Study Rooms and Spaces | South Dakota State University
cards.access_notes: SDSU describes first-floor, entryway, and second- and third-floor collaborative options; no reservation rule is stated.

cards.title: Hilton M. Briggs Library
cards.subtitle: Individual rooms, group rooms and open main-floor seating
cards.notes: Use a second-floor individual room for private outlet-equipped work, reserve a group room when needed, or work at the main-floor computers and printers.
cards.short_summary: A library setting with private rooms, reservable group rooms and open study seating.
cards.evidence_claim: SDSU lists individual rooms with outlets and no reservation, group rooms for reservation, and main-floor open study space with computers and printers.
cards.source_title: Campus Study Rooms and Spaces | South Dakota State University
cards.access_notes: Individual study rooms are on the second floor and require no reservation. Group rooms are throughout the library and are reservable.

cards.title: Multicultural Affairs and Accessibility
cards.subtitle: Second floor of the University Student Union
cards.notes: Bring solo or small-group work to the varied chairs, couches and high-top seating; ask the OMAA senior secretary if you need the reservable conference room.
cards.short_summary: A low-volume Union study setting with varied seating, computers and a reservable conference room.
cards.evidence_claim: SDSU describes low-volume individual and group workspace with computers, varied seating and a conference room reservable through the OMAA senior secretary.
cards.source_title: Campus Study Rooms and Spaces | South Dakota State University
cards.access_notes: Located on the Union's second floor; conference-room reservations are handled by the OMAA senior secretary.

cards.title: Oscar Larson Performing Arts Center
cards.subtitle: Study spaces on the east side of campus
cards.notes: Use the mix of chairs, couches and high-top seating to match your task, with natural light and room to work individually or alongside a group.
cards.short_summary: A naturally lit performing-arts building with flexible seating for solo or group work.
cards.evidence_claim: SDSU states that the center has natural lighting, low volume, varied seating and space for individual and group work.
cards.source_title: Campus Study Rooms and Spaces | South Dakota State University
cards.access_notes: SDSU identifies multiple study spaces in the building; no reservation requirement is stated.

cards.title: Raven Precision Agriculture Center
cards.subtitle: First- and second-floor collaborative nooks and lounge
cards.notes: Use a collaborative nook for a small team with a whiteboard and casting monitor, or select the lounge or low-top tables for lighter individual work.
cards.short_summary: Small-team nooks and individual tables with documented outlet access.
cards.evidence_claim: SDSU says the center is open to all students and offers collaborative nooks with outlets, whiteboards and casting monitors, plus a lounge and low-top tables.
cards.source_title: Campus Study Rooms and Spaces | South Dakota State University
cards.access_notes: Open to all students. Collaborative nooks are on the first and second floors.

cards.title: University Student Union
cards.subtitle: Multiple study settings in the center of campus
cards.notes: Use the Union as a central study stop with several seating areas; it also places dining, Jackrabbit Central and Multicultural Affairs and Accessibility nearby.
cards.short_summary: A centrally located building with multiple study spots and campus services under one roof.
cards.evidence_claim: SDSU states that the University Student Union has plenty of places to study individually or with friends and houses multiple offices and dining options.
cards.source_title: Campus Study Rooms and Spaces | South Dakota State University
cards.access_notes: SDSU identifies multiple study areas in the Union; access and reservation terms vary by area.

cards.title: Jacks Place
cards.subtitle: Lower level of the University Student Union
cards.notes: Head to the lower level when you need a lower-volume table or seat with outlet access, keeping your work session inside the central campus Union.
cards.short_summary: A lower-level Union study area with varied seating and outlets.
cards.evidence_claim: SDSU lists Jacks Place on the Union's lower level as a low-volume study area with various seating options and outlets.
cards.source_title: Campus Study Rooms and Spaces | South Dakota State University
cards.access_notes: Located on the University Student Union lower level; no reservation rule is stated.
